title: Benchmark provenance layer and versioned model-pinning adapter for profile publishing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: When publishing performance profiles for newly onboarded models we lack a first-class provenance and pinning mechanism. This causes two issues: (1) downstream rollouts can't deterministically reference the exact artifact + dataset/prompt snapshot that produced a profile, and (2) eval runners with different sampling/transformation layers may claim incompatible profiles.

Goal: Implement a lightweight provenance layer that records the full benchmark artifact (model version id, quantization variant, seed, dataset snapshot id, prompt template hash, runner version) and a versioned 'pinning adapter' that can map a profile to fallback-compatible model variants at runtime. The adapter should live inside the benchmark harness so profiles published to the catalog include both metadata and a signed provenance manifest.

Scope:
- Add a provenance manifest schema to the harness output (JSON manifest with stable keys).
- Emit manifest alongside performance summary and store in artifact registry (S3 path + checksum).
- Extend the profile publisher to include the manifest and a signed manifest fingerprint.
- Build a pinning adapter library (py) that: resolves model pins to candidate variants, exposes compatibility predicates (max sequence length, kv-cache layout, quantization family), and produces deterministic fallback chains.
- Backfill compatibility checks into existing eval runners so they assert manifest compatibility (warning or fail based on policy).

Out of scope: the full UI surface in Console for browsing provenance (tracked by a separate ticket). Onboarding automation for private installations will be follow-up work.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark harness emits a provenance manifest JSON for every profile run containing model_version, model_variant, quantization, dataset_snapshot_id, prompt_hash, runner_version, random_seed, and config_hash.
Published profiles in the catalog include a pointer to the manifest and a signed manifest fingerprint stored with the artifact.
Pinning adapter resolves a profile to at least one compatible fallback variant when the primary variant is unavailable and logs the resolution path.
Eval runners validate manifest compatibility and produce a non-zero warning metric when they auto-fallback; failures must surface in the harness CI.
Unit and integration tests cover manifest generation, signing, registry upload, and the adapter resolution logic.

comments: 2026-03-10 Aisha: Kickoff — wrote initial design notes and proposed manifest fields. Decided to keep schema flat and stable to avoid future churn.

2026-03-11 Diego: Prototype of manifest writer added in branch feat/provenance-manifest; uploading to s3://redwood-benchmarks/provenance/ with uuid-based keys. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmark-harness/pull/489
2026-03-11 Priya Shah: Reviewed schema and raised concern about prompt_hash collisions for templated prompts. We agreed to include both prompt_template_hash and prompt_variant_index when applicable.

2026-03-12 Diego: Started pinning adapter implementation. Two fallback strategies under consideration: (A) relax quantization family constraint but require same attention layout, (B) allow different quantization if KL divergence test on a small validation set passes. Need architecture decision for default policy.
2026-03-12 Aisha: For initial rollout default policy will choose strategy (A) for safety; (B) will be gated behind a runtime flag and additional QA. Added ticket to follow up on auto-KL verification.
links: Related Linear: ENG-71234 (benchmark harness runner fanout)
notes: Manifest must be stable across repeated runs for the same inputs; include deterministic sorting for list fields and canonical JSON writing.
Use the existing key management flow for signing manifests; if not available, use a short-lived HMAC key stored in secrets manager as a stopgap.
Pinning adapter should be pure python and lightweight so it can be vendored into other services (console, onprem publisher).
We should include a small 'compatibility matrix' in the manifest summarizing runner features used (e.g., kvcache_version, attention_layout).
Make sure the harness CI can simulate model unavailability and exercise fallback resolution in the adapter.
